_comment: DECLARATIVE KWin window rules — data-driven, consumed by window-rules.nix. Rules are applied with kwriteconfig6 at activation rather than by owning ~/.config/kwinrulesrc outright: KWin REWRITES that file whenever a rule is edited in System Settings, so a /nix/store symlink there would be replaced by a real file on first GUI edit and the declaration would silently stop applying — the exact failure konsolerc, Profile 1.profile and baloofilerc all hit (see app_especific/konsole.nix). Setting individual keys instead re-asserts ours on every switch while leaving any rule the user adds by hand untouched.
_desktop_ids_doc: KWin identifies virtual desktops by the Id_N strings in ~/.config/kwinrc [Desktops], NOT by position. This machine: Id_1=Desktop_1 (Desk1) … Id_5=Desktop_5 (Desk5). Plasma 6 dropped kstart's --desktop flag (kstart 6.2.5 has only --desktopfile/--application), so launching a window onto a specific desktop is no longer possible from the command line — a window rule is the supported mechanism.
_desktopsrule_doc: KWin rule 'set' modes: 1=Apply Initially, 2=Force, 3=Remember, 4=Apply Now, 5=Force Temporarily. Force (2) is used so the window cannot drift to whichever desktop happened to be active when the build started. Apply Initially (1) is used for a DEFAULT landing spot the user is free to move afterward — the distinction that matters for the waydroid-default-desktop rule below.
_titlematch_doc: 0=unimportant, 1=exact, 2=substring, 3=regex — KWin's Rules::StringMatch, where UnimportantMatch is 0 BECAUSE 0 is what an unset field reads as (an unset title must mean 'don't care', not 'exact-match the empty string'). CORRECTED 2026-08-24: this line previously claimed '0=exact … 3=unimportant', exactly inverted, and BOTH rules below were encoded against that wrong table — so waydroid-default-desktop asked for 'class unimportant + title regex ""' and never applied, and build-progress-windows asked for 'class regex "" + title substring "A|B"' (a literal, not an alternation) and can never match either. Verified live against KWin 6.2.5 with kdotool: wmclassmatch=1 + wmclass=Waydroid places the window, wmclassmatch=0 does not. 'unimportant' is not a lower-priority match, it is OFF — the field is not evaluated at all, which is how a rule that matches on wmclass alone disables the title condition rather than exact-matching against an empty string.
_wmclass_doc: wmclass/wmclassmatch/wmclasscomplete use the same match-mode enum as titlematch (see _titlematch_doc). wmclass is the window's app-id on Wayland (WM_CLASS on X11) — steadier than title for an app whose title changes with what it is displaying, e.g. Waydroid's title tracking whichever Android app has focus. wmclasscomplete=false matches the resource class only; true also requires the resource NAME to match, which native Wayland toplevels usually set identically to the class anyway.

rules._comment: THREE windows, one rule. build.sh opens a Konsole via its own konsole_wrap AND flakes-switch-progress-logs opens another, and switch-progress.sh adds a kdialog — all three used to land on whatever desktop was focused, burying the work in progress. Desk3 is deliberate: default-session.json leaves desktop 3 empty (1=konsole+my-konsole, 2=kate, 5=dolphin+brave, 4=reserved for waydroid's default landing spot), so builds get a dedicated space and never cover the terminal that launched them.
rules.title: Nix Switch Progress|NixOS switch —

rules.description: Waydroid -> Desk4 (forced: late Wayland app_id defeats Apply Initially; still not autostarted)
rules._comment: Desk4 was Dolphin+Brave until the desk5 split (2026-08-22): everything that used to live on desk4 moved to desk5, freeing desk4 as Waydroid's dedicated space instead of a fifth generic desktop. desktopsrule was 1 (Apply Initially) so the window had a default landing PLACE the user could still drag away. That is not achievable for this window and is now 2 (Force): Waydroid is a native WAYLAND toplevel whose app_id arrives AFTER the surface is mapped, so at KWin's initial rule pass the class is still empty, the wmclass condition cannot match, and Apply Initially is already spent by the time app_id lands. Verified live on KWin 6.2.5 — Exact+ApplyInitially left the window on the current desktop every time, Exact+Force put it on Desktop_4 every time. Force re-evaluates continuously, which is the only mode that survives a late app_id. Cost of Force: the window is pinned to Desk4 and cannot be dragged to another desktop. There is still no autostart / systemd service for Waydroid anywhere (see containers-cloud/waydroid-container.nix) — this rule only fires once a window actually opens. Matches by wmclass, not title: Waydroid's window title tracks whichever Android app has focus, but its native Wayland app-id is the constant 'Waydroid' (see waydroid-container.nix's StartupWMClass).
